questions.prompt: The Claude docs describe a customer support job. What do they call it?

options.text: A collection of multiple different tasks.
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs call customer support "a collection of multiple different tasks" and say to break it down before you start.

options.text: One single task that AI can do from start to end.
options.explanation: The docs say the opposite. It is many tasks, and they talk about AI doing only "portions" of the work.

options.text: A job that only people can do, with no AI at all.
options.explanation: The docs talk about using AI to "automate portions" of support work. So some parts can use AI.

questions.prompt: What do the OpenAI docs recommend before AI outputs are used in practice?

options.text: Nothing, as long as the output sounds sure and clear.
options.explanation: A sure tone is not a check. The docs recommend a human review.

options.text: A human reviews them, especially in high-stakes areas.
options.explanation: Right. The docs recommend "having a human review outputs before they are used in practice", and say it is especially critical in high-stakes domains.

options.text: A second AI model reviews them instead of a person.
options.explanation: The docs ask for a human review, and the human needs the original material to check against.

questions.prompt: What do the ChatGPT docs say about legal, financial and medical decisions?

options.text: They need expert review, and AI supports judgment without replacing it.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say these decisions "require appropriate expert review" and to use ChatGPT "to support informed judgment, not replace it."

options.text: AI can make them alone, if your first message is long and clear.
options.explanation: A good message does not make the answer expert advice. These decisions need an expert.

options.text: Chat apps are not allowed to talk about these topics at all.
options.explanation: The docs don't say that. They say the decisions need expert review.
